hero.filename: Photograph of the Greentree Tavern in Ste Genevieve MO.jpg
hero.caption: This is a photograph of the Greentree Tavern, sometimes called the Nicolas Janis House, in Ste. Geneviève, Missouri. It was built c. 1790 by Nicolas Janis.  It is an example of Post-on-sill—poteaux-sur-solle construction.

images.filename: Carpenter marks on Green Tree Tavern. (1a858027-5c4b-4617-9445-aa13b5155942).JPG
images.caption:
A horizontal beam joined with two vertical beams, each with Roman numerals carved into them.
Carpenter marks are found on several areas of the Green Tree Tavern. These helped the workers construct the house.

images.filename: Carpenter marks under porch of the Green Tree Tavern (342c9e75-08ed-4672-86fa-c2ff13499db4).JPG
images.caption:
A horizontal wooden beam with Roman numerals 'VIII' and 'XXXXXVI'.
A master carpenter would label joints with Roman numerals so that the workers knew what logs to connect. One of the many places at Green Tree Tavern to find these marks is under the porch.
Keywords: vertical log; Ste. Genevieve; ste. genevieve nhp; colonial french architecture; Green Tree Tavern; poteaux-sur-sole

images.caption:
Room with wooden floors and ceiling. On the left is a wood mantle and fireplace and an open door. An open door is in the center of the room and through the door other rooms can be seen. The walls are green under a chair rail and white above.
The family that lived in Green Tree Tavern would have occupied this room and two adjoining bedrooms on the left.
Keywords: Bauvais-Amoureux House; colonial french architecture; Ste. Genevieve; ste. genevieve nhp; Green Tree Tavern; homes; tavern

images.caption:
Underside of a wooden porch. Two beams meet in a zig-zag pattern and two pegs hold them together.
Lap joints were used in the construction of the porch ceiling. The joint was held together by driving two dowels to connect the two wooden beams.
Keywords: vertical log; Ste. Genevieve; ste. genevieve nhp; colonial french architecture; Green Tree Tavern; tavern; homes; poteaux-sur-sole
